## Overview

Orchestration improvements built on top of the AI assistant infrastructure (#8319). Four main themes: sequential fallback mode for non-parallel platforms, result-file-based parallel gate coordination, quality hardening across agents and skills, and reliability fixes from the June workshop.

---

## Changes by area

### Orchestrator
- Add `--sequential` flag to force sequential execution of all parallel agent groups — use on platforms that don't support parallel Agent spawning (e.g. GitHub Copilot)
- Document parallel vs sequential execution modes (~40–50% cycle time reduction in parallel mode)
- Add **Mandatory Pipeline Gates** section — grooming, label/assignee, and `gh pr ready` are explicitly non-skippable with a model-agnostic enforcement table
- Add explicit continuation warning after Step 6 (draft PR creation): the draft PR is the **midpoint** of the pipeline, not the end — models were stopping here on non-Claude platforms

### Agent model routing & metadata
- Add `model:`, `maxTurns:`, and `color:` frontmatter to all agents for explicit per-agent routing:
  - `backend-agent`, `frontend-agent`, `lead-reviewer`: `sonnet` / 60, 60, 25 turns
  - `grooming-agent`, `e2e-qa-tester`: 40 turns
  - `qa-engineer`: 35 turns (also removes `mcp__playwright` from tools — delegated to `e2e-qa-tester`)
  - `challenger`: 20 turns
  - `ticket-writer`: `haiku` / 15 turns
  - `release-agent`: `haiku` / 10 turns

### Parallel quality gates via result files
- `backend-agent`, `frontend-agent`, `lead-reviewer`, `qa-engineer`, and DOD L2 skill each write a JSON result file to `.TemporaryItems/Issues/wp-rocket/issue-<N>/contracts/` before returning
- Files are read by the orchestrator for routing decisions, enabling true parallel gate coordination without polling

### Event emission
- `backend-agent` and `frontend-agent` emit `agent_start` and `implementation_complete` events to `orchestrator-events.jsonl`
- `lead-reviewer` emits inline comment events and a review summary event to the JSONL stream instead of posting directly via `gh pr comment`
- `qa-engineer` emits a `post_comment_to_pr` GitHub operation event after generating the report
- `ticket-writer` emits a `create_issue` event before calling `gh issue create`

### Grooming-agent improvements
- Accept a `complexity_signal` input from the orchestrator and adapt reasoning depth accordingly (5–8 turns for XS, 30–40 for XL)
- Require a PR splitting plan for L/XL efforts: vertical slices only (each slice ships a complete behavior — data layer + logic + tests), no horizontal-layer splits
- Add `effort_used` and `pr_splitting_plan` fields to the return JSON

### QA-engineer improvements
- Add expanded UI keyword triggers for Strategy B: if issue title/PR body/acceptance criteria mention `display`, `visual`, `UI`, `admin`, `notice`, `button`, `toggle`, `checkbox`, `field`, `renders`, `appears`, `shows`, `user sees` — Strategy B is mandatory
- Add pre-execution safety check: if Strategy B was not selected but the PR clearly involves UI changes, pause and re-select before running
- Renumber steps for clarity

### DOD skill hardening
- Add anti-rationalization table: preempts common agent rationalizations for skipping checks
- Strengthen Check 2: a WARN for a missing test requires an explicit written justification; "follow-up ticket" is a FAIL, not a WARN
- Add `phpcs:fix` auto-fix guidance: run `composer phpcs:fix` then `composer phpcs-changed` — never file-by-file
- Add Check 6 — File scope compliance (Layer 1 only): compare changed files against declared `file_scope` in `tasks.json`
- Add result file write for Layer 2

### e2e skill
- Add anti-rationalization table: preempts skipping the environment boot or the primary scenario

### Challenger
- Add Hyrum's Law angle (#6): flag any observable behavior change (hook timing, filter return shapes, cache headers, admin notice order) as a potential breaking change

### AGENTS.md
- Add five operating principles that apply to every agent before skill-specific guidance

### Workshop feedback (June 2026)

**#1 — Remove GitKraken MCP** (`issue-workflow/SKILL.md`): shell is the primary approach; GitHub MCP listed as optional fallback. GitKraken rows removed entirely — it blocked users without GitKraken installed.

**#2 — Explicit PR-issue link** (`release-agent`): PR body now gets a standalone `Closes #N` line immediately after the AI notice. GitHub's parser requires a standalone line (not buried in prose) to reliably link and auto-close the issue.

**#3 — Label & assignee robustness** (`release-agent`): check if `Made by AI` label exists before applying; create it if missing instead of skipping silently. Verify label + assignee actually appear on the PR after `gh pr edit` and retry once on failure.

**#4/#5 — Grooming and pipeline step enforcement** (`orchestrator`): the Mandatory Pipeline Gates table makes grooming, label/assignee, and `gh pr ready` non-skippable at the instruction level — applies to any model running the orchestrator.

**#6 — Pipeline stops after draft PR** (`orchestrator`): Step 6 ended at a natural-looking `---` boundary; models without full context were treating the draft PR as the finish line. Added an explicit blockquote warning at the Step 6/7 seam.

**#9 — Playwright spec trustworthiness** (`e2e-qa-tester`): before deleting temp spec files, capture full source and embed it verbatim in the report under a `<details>` collapsible block + `specs_content[]` JSON field. Reviewers can verify what was tested even after the temp file is deleted.

**#10 — Copilot-level review depth** (`lead-reviewer`): new Step 2.5 — Cross-file impact analysis. After reading the diff, grep for every changed symbol across the codebase, read consumer files outside the diff, and check for broken callers, missing sibling state updates, and hook signature side effects. This is the class of issue Copilot catches that diff-only review misses (e.g. unsetting `analytics_enabled` silently breaking `Data.php` and `Tracking.php`).

### Fix
- `release-agent`: fix shell quoting bug in the `TRAILER` rebase `--exec` command

---

## Base branch

Targets `develop` (base `chore/add-ai-assistant` was squash-merged as #8319).

I'm mapping out the remaining PRs: parallel gates with result file writes across the backend and frontend agents plus orchestrator updates, grooming improvements with complexity signals, QA enhancements for UI triggers and step renumbering, DOD hardening with anti-rationalization checks and PHPCS guidance, and finally the e2e and challenger updates.

---
# Pull Request Guidelines
Instructions for creating and reviewing pull requests in wp-rocket

## Branch Naming Convention

### Required Format
Branch names MUST follow these patterns based on the type of work:

- **Bug fixes**: `fix/{GitHub-issue-ID}-{description}`
- Example: `fix/1234-resolve-cache-clearing-issue`

- **Enhancements**: `enhancement/{GitHub-issue-ID}-{GitHub-issue-title}`
- Example: `enhancement/5678-improve-css-minification-performance`

- **Tests**: `test/{GitHub-issue-ID}-{GitHub-issue-title}`
- Example: `test/9012-add-unit-tests-for-lazyload-module`

### Branch Naming Rules
- Use lowercase letters
- Replace spaces with hyphens (`-`)
- Keep descriptions concise but descriptive
- Always include the GitHub issue ID
- For bug fixes, use a brief description of what's being fixed
- For enhancements and tests, use the GitHub issue title (or abbreviated version)

### Examples
- ✅ `fix/3421-cdn-url-generation-error`
- ✅ `enhancement/2890-add-webp-support`
- ✅ `test/4567-critical-css-generation`
- ❌ `bugfix-cache` (missing issue ID and wrong prefix)
- ❌ `Fix/123-Cache-Issue` (wrong capitalization)
- ❌ `enhancement-new-feature` (missing issue ID)

## When Creating Pull Requests

### Template Reference
- MUST follow the complete PR template from `wp-media/.github/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`
- Template location: https://github.com/wp-media/.github/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
- YOU MUST read and use the latest version of this template for every PR

### CRITICAL: Exact Section Headings Required
- DO NOT modify, rename, or abbreviate any section headings from the template
- The PR validation workflow (`pr-checklist-action`) performs strict string matching on section headings
- Examples of what NOT to do:
- ❌ "QA Scope" instead of "Affected Features & Quality Assurance Scope"
- ❌ "Docs" instead of "Documentation"
- ❌ "Testing" instead of "What was tested"
- ❌ Any variation in capitalization, punctuation, or wording
- ALWAYS copy section headings exactly as they appear in the template
- You may ONLY modify the content under each heading, never the heading itself

### Required Sections
The validation workflow checks for these EXACT headings:
- `# Description`
- `## Type of change`
- `## Detailed scenario`
- `### What was tested`
- `### How to test`
- `### Affected Features & Quality Assurance Scope`
